quickstart.title: Quick Start (Onboarding)
quickstart.description: Step-by-step unboxing and onboarding guide to get your Zenso frame up and running.
quickstart.intro: Setting up your Zenso frame requires zero coding and takes less than two minutes.
quickstart.step1_desc: Turn on the power switch located on the rear panel. The e-paper display will cycle through an initial waveform wipe and present the onboarding screen.
quickstart.step2_desc:
On your smartphone, open your Wi-Fi settings:
1. Connect to the temporary hotspot broadcast by the frame (SSID: `Zenso-Setup`).
2. A captive portal will appear automatically.
3. Select your home 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network and enter your network password.
   *(Note: 5 GHz-only bands are not supported by the 802.11 b/g/n radio).*
quickstart.step3_desc: Once connected to the internet, the frame fetches device authorization and displays an authentic pairing QR code on its 7.3" screen. Scan it with any smartphone camera to open the Zenso management portal.
quickstart.step4_desc:
In the portal, pick what to display:
- **Family Photo Albums**: Personal memories and curated artwork with automatic orientation and e-ink color dithering.
- **Ambient Weather**: Live conditions, forecasts, and barometric trends.
- **Calendar & Agenda**: Google Calendar or CalDAV events.
- **Bento Grids**: Multi-widget layouts configured without writing a line of code.
quickstart.step5_desc: Your frame will update quietly according to your preferred schedule (e.g., hourly during the day, asleep overnight) and immediately enter ultra-low power deep sleep (< 15 µA) between refreshes, preserving battery and home tranquility.

overview.title: Overview
overview.description: Zenso is a cordless 7-color e-paper smart frame that stays out of your way — no light, no noise, months of battery life.
overview.intro: Zenso is a cordless 7-color e-paper smart frame designed to fit quietly into your home. It displays family photos, weather, and calendar events without emitting a single photon of light — just like a print on the wall. When the battery runs out, the last image stays on the screen indefinitely. Plug in USB-C when you're ready to refresh.
overview.refresh_desc: Set your own schedule in the web panel — hourly updates during the day, complete silence overnight. The frame wakes up only when needed and immediately goes back to sleep, so it never disrupts your home.
overview.local_desc: Zenso works with the official Zenso Cloud out of the box, or you can run your own self-hosted stack on your home network using the provided Docker image — zero telemetry, no subscriptions, complete privacy.

faq.title: Non-Technical FAQ & Daily Experience
faq.description: Frequently asked questions about battery life, light emission, Wi-Fi networks, and everyday usage.
faq.q1: Does the frame emit light in the bedroom or at night?
faq.a1:
**No, absolutely none.**

Zenso uses reflective electronic paper with physical color pigment microcapsules. It produces zero backlight, zero blue light, and zero glare, looking just like museum-grade archival paper print under ambient room lighting. At night when the room lights are off, the frame is completely dark.
faq.q2: What happens when the battery runs out?
faq.a2:
**The image stays on the screen forever.**

The ACeP e-paper technology is bi-stable. This means the micro-pigments stay locked in position indefinitely with zero electrical power. The last displayed image or family photo remains crisp and visible forever until you plug in a standard USB-C charger.
faq.a3:
**Standard 2.4 GHz 802.11 b/g/n networks.**

Zenso connects to standard 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi (supported by virtually all home broadband routers). 5 GHz-only bands are not supported by the hardware radio. If your home Wi-Fi broadcasts separate SSID names for 2.4 GHz and 5 GHz, connect to the 2.4 GHz network during initial onboarding.
faq.q4: Can multiple family members send photos to the frame?
faq.a4:
**Yes.**

You can share your frame's private invite link or pairing QR code with trusted family members through [panel.zenso.ink](https://panel.zenso.ink) so they can contribute photos to your shared album without needing technical knowledge.

overview.title: Overview & Philosophy
overview.description: Discover the calm technology, Japandi aesthetics, and paper-like tranquility of the Zenso smart frame.
overview.lead: Zenso was created to bring information and art into your home without the stress, bright glow, and constant notifications of conventional displays. Built around the principles of **calm technology**, Zenso stays out of your way until you choose to look at it.
overview.philosophy_title: The Spirit of Japandi & Calm Living
overview.philosophy_body: Modern living spaces are saturated with bright LED and OLED screens competing for human attention. Zenso embodies the Japanese concept of *Ma* (negative space) and Scandinavian functionalism. It harmonizes with your interior, acting as a piece of digital furniture that breathes with your daily rhythm.
overview.display_body: At the heart of every frame lies an Advanced Color e-Paper (ACeP) display featuring physical color microcapsules. By moving red, green, blue, yellow, black, and white pigments with microscopic voltage pulses, the screen reflects natural ambient light. It emits **zero photons**, produces zero blue light in the dark, and causes zero eyestrain.
overview.craftsmanship_body: Every frame enclosure is CNC-machined from solid European oak and finished by hand with natural protective oils. There are no visible wires, no intrusive plastic bezels, and no glowing status LEDs on the front face.

quickstart.title: Unboxing & Wi-Fi Setup
quickstart.description: Get your Zenso frame unboxed, connected to Wi-Fi via captive portal, and paired in under three minutes.
quickstart.lead: Setting up your Zenso frame requires no technical background and takes less than three minutes using any smartphone or laptop.
quickstart.step1_body: Slide the power switch on the rear panel to the **ON** position. The e-paper display will cycle through a clean waveform wipe and present the onboarding welcome screen.
quickstart.step2_body: On your smartphone or computer, open your Wi-Fi network settings and connect to the temporary network named **`Zenso-Setup`**.
quickstart.step3_body: A captive portal web page will open automatically. Choose your home 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi network from the list, enter your password, and save. *(Note: 5 GHz-only bands are not supported by the hardware radio).*
quickstart.step4_body: Once connected to the internet, the frame will fetch authorization and display an authentic pairing QR code. Scan it with your phone's camera to claim the frame in your Zenso Web Panel.

panel_basics.title: Managing Your Frame
panel_basics.description: Learn how to use the Zenso Web Panel to monitor frame battery levels, network status, and screen assignments.
panel_basics.lead: The Zenso Web Panel at [panel.zenso.ink](https://panel.zenso.ink) (or your private self-hosted instance) serves as the central command center for all your frames.
panel_basics.access_body: Log in with your user credentials or passkey. Your dashboard displays all claimed frames with real-time telemetry, device nicknames, and their currently active display screens.
panel_basics.telemetry_body: Each frame card reports its current battery percentage, estimated remaining battery lifespan, Wi-Fi RSSI signal strength, and exact timestamp of the last successful synchronization check-in.
panel_basics.screen_assignment_body: Switch screens instantly or set up automated rotation schedules. Changes configured in the panel are pushed to your frame during its next scheduled wake-up cycle.

screens_and_layouts.title: Screens & Layouts
screens_and_layouts.description: Combine multiple widgets on a single screen using split-screen presets and rotation management.
screens_and_layouts.lead: A Screen represents a visual canvas displayed on your e-paper frame. Zenso allows you to divide screens into multiple independent widget slots.
screens_and_layouts.layouts_body:
Choose from optimized layout presets:
- **Full Screen**: A single immersive slot occupying 100% of the canvas (ideal for photography or monthly calendars).
- **Split 50/50**: Two balanced side-by-side columns.
- **Top & Bottom**: Two horizontal rows.
- **2x2 Grid**: Four compact quadrants for dense ambient dashboards (e.g. clock, weather, agenda, and quotes).
screens_and_layouts.rotation_body: Whether your frame is hung on a wall in landscape or resting on an easel in portrait, set the rotation to 0°, 90°, 180°, or 270°. The layout engine automatically transposes coordinates to prevent distortion.
screens_and_layouts.preview_body: The panel provides an instant, pixel-accurate live preview showing exactly how each slot and widget will render on your specific display resolution.

refresh_and_battery.title: Refresh Cadence & Battery Life
refresh_and_battery.description: Optimize refresh intervals, configure night sleep schedules, and achieve months of cordless operation.
refresh_and_battery.lead: Because electrophoretic displays require electrical power **only when changing pigments**, Zenso operates cordlessly for months on a single USB-C charge.
refresh_and_battery.cadence_body: Adjust your update interval according to the content you display. A photo frame or calendar updates perfectly every 1 to 2 hours, whereas an ambient status board can refresh every 15 minutes.
refresh_and_battery.sleep_body: Configure a quiet night schedule (e.g., 23:00 to 07:00). During these hours, the microcontroller remains in ultra-low-power deep sleep (< 15 µA), saving energy when no one is awake.
refresh_and_battery.charging_body: When the battery reaches 15%, the panel notifies you. Simply plug in any standard USB-C charger for 2 to 3 hours to restore full charge for the next several months.

plugins_image.title: Photo Frame Plugin
plugins_image.description: Display family photos, curated art collections, and ambient photography with cover and contain fit modes.
plugins_image.lead: The official Photo Frame plugin transforms your Zenso frame into an exhibition of personal memories and timeless artwork.
plugins_image.config_body: Provide a direct image URL or select an uploaded album in the panel. The plugin automatically caches the image and schedules updates according to your preference.
plugins_image.fitting_body:
- **Cover (Fill)**: Scales the image to fill the entire slot without black bars, gently cropping overflowing edges.
- **Contain (Fit)**: Fits the entire image within the slot borders, preserving 100% of the original photo framing.
plugins_image.dithering_body: Photographs are processed with perceptual color palette quantization tailored to ACeP pigment capsules. An optional high-contrast monochrome mode is also available for dramatic black-and-white portraits.

plugins_calendar.title: Calendar Plugin
plugins_calendar.description: Sync Google Calendar, Apple iCloud, and CalDAV feeds onto your desk with calm, non-intrusive visibility.
plugins_calendar.lead: Keep your family or workday schedule visible at a glance without notification dings or glowing monitor tabs.
plugins_calendar.sync_body: Paste any standard secret or public `.ics` link from Google Calendar, Apple iCloud Calendar, Microsoft Outlook, or Nextcloud into the plugin settings.
plugins_calendar.views_body:
Select between multiple clean views:
- **Agenda / List**: Shows upcoming events for today and tomorrow.
- **Month View**: Classic grid showing the current month with highlighted busy days.
- **Day View**: Detailed timeline of hourly commitments.
plugins_calendar.customization_body: Toggle between 12-hour and 24-hour time notations, hide all-day events, and assign distinctive color badges to differentiate family members or work categories.

troubleshooting_faq.title: Troubleshooting & Maintenance
troubleshooting_faq.description: Solutions for Wi-Fi reconnection, battery care, and clearing display ghosting with a full white wipe.
troubleshooting_faq.lead: Practical maintenance steps and solutions for everyday questions about your Zenso smart frame.
troubleshooting_faq.wifi_body: If you change your home router or Wi-Fi password, turn the frame power switch off and on twice rapidly, or press the internal reset button on the baseboard to re-broadcast the `Zenso-Setup` hotspot.
troubleshooting_faq.ghosting_body: Electronic paper can occasionally retain faint shadow traces after hundreds of partial updates. In the web panel, click **Force Full Refresh** to cycle through an inverted waveform wipe, restoring pristine contrast.
troubleshooting_faq.battery_body: The internal Lithium-Ion battery includes built-in overcharge and over-discharge protection. For maximum battery longevity over years of use, recharge when the battery indicator reaches 15-20%.

overview.title: Local-First Architecture
overview.description: Understand Zenso's Local-First philosophy, complete data sovereignty, and open developer ecosystem.
overview.lead: Zenso is built from the ground up on the principle of **data sovereignty**. Your photos, schedules, and device telemetry remain strictly within your local home network unless you explicitly configure external services.
overview.local_first_body: Unlike typical commercial smart displays that become paperweights when remote servers go down, Zenso treats your local network as the primary source of truth. The frame can communicate directly with your self-hosted Docker instance on your home server or NAS.
overview.licensing_body: We provide official, free-to-use Docker images for the complete backend stack. Meanwhile, the microcontroller firmware (GPLv3), public schemas (Apache 2.0), Vite development plugin (MIT), and starter templates (MIT) are fully open source.
overview.stack_body:
The architecture comprises three functional layers:
1. **Core Services**: High-performance backend handling device sessions, layout rendering, and image quantization.
2. **Web Panel**: Responsive configuration interface accessible via browser on desktop and mobile.
3. **Firmware & Widgets**: Microcontroller runtime and Liquid-based widget templates.

docker_setup.title: Docker & Self-Hosting
docker_setup.description: Deploy the official Zenso API and Panel stack on your HomeLab or NAS using Docker Compose.
docker_setup.lead: Running Zenso on your local infrastructure takes less than two minutes using Docker Compose.
docker_setup.compose_body:
Create a directory for Zenso and save the following configuration file:

```yaml
services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: zenso
      POSTGRES_USER: zenso
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-changeme_secure_password}
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data

  zenso-api:
    image: ghcr.io/zensoink/zenso-api:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      PORT: 3000
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://zenso:${DB_PASSWORD:-changeme_secure_password}@postgres:5432/zenso
      FRONTEND_URL: http://${HOST_IP:-localhost}:8080
      ZENSO_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS: "true"
    depends_on:
      - postgres

  zenso-panel:
    image: ghcr.io/zensoink/zenso-panel:latest
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    depends_on:
      - zenso-api

volumes:
  postgres_data:
```
docker_setup.run_body:
Run the container stack in detached mode:

```bash
docker compose up -d
```

Verify that all containers are healthy by checking `docker compose ps`.
docker_setup.storage_body: All user settings, screens, layouts, and widget configurations are securely stored inside the named Docker volume `postgres_data`. Regular volume backups guarantee simple migration between servers.

environment_variables.title: Environment Variables
environment_variables.description: Reference guide for configuring ports, database URLs, CORS, and private LAN access in .env.
environment_variables.lead: Configure your Zenso container deployment through standard environment variables defined in your `.env` file.
environment_variables.core_body:
| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `PORT` | `3000` | Port on which the API listens for panel and device connections. |
| `DATABASE_URL` | — | Connection string for PostgreSQL (e.g. `postgresql://user:pass@host:5432/db`). |
| `FRONTEND_URL` | `http://localhost:8080` | Canonical URL of the panel used for CORS validation and invite links. |
| `SESSION_SECRET` | — | Secure cryptographic salt for signing session tokens. |
environment_variables.network_body:
| Variable | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ZENSO_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORKS` | `false` | When set to `true`, permits widgets and plugins to query internal RFC1918 IPs (e.g. Home Assistant at `192.168.1.50`) without triggering SSRF protection blocks. |

cold_boot_setup.title: Cold-Boot Setup Wizard
cold_boot_setup.description: Initialize a new instance securely using the setup token generated in Docker container logs.
cold_boot_setup.lead: When a new Zenso instance starts for the first time, it enforces a cryptographic bootstrap protocol to prevent unauthorized claiming.
cold_boot_setup.token_body:
Inspect the container logs of the API container to retrieve the generated single-use token:

```bash
docker compose logs zenso-api | grep "SETUP TOKEN"
```

You will see an entry similar to: `ZENSO_SETUP_TOKEN: zenso_sec_9f81a7b...`
cold_boot_setup.wizard_body:
Open your web browser and navigate to:

`http://<SERVER_IP>:8080/setup`

Paste your setup token and click **Verify Instance**.
cold_boot_setup.claim_body: Specify the administrator email and a strong password. Once submitted, the token is permanently invalidated, and you are logged into your sovereign Zenso dashboard.

plugin_architecture.title: Widget Plugin Architecture
plugin_architecture.description: Learn how Zenso widgets use LiquidJS templates, server-side headless rendering, and JSON schemas.
plugin_architecture.lead: Zenso widgets are authorable using standard, approachable web technologies: HTML, CSS, and the LiquidJS template engine.
plugin_architecture.rendering_body: Instead of running a heavy JavaScript browser engine on the low-power microcontroller, widgets are rendered server-side. The renderer populates the Liquid template with live data, applies responsive CSS, and rasterizes the canvas into an optimized multi-color e-paper bitmap.
plugin_architecture.structure_body:
A valid Zenso plugin contains the following core files:

```
my-zenso-widget/
├── manifest.json      # Metadata, configuration schema, and data sources
├── index.liquid       # Visual template with Liquid placeholders
├── style.css          # Scoped CSS stylesheet
└── mock/              # Sample mock data for local development
    └── plugin.json
```
plugin_architecture.data_flow_body: Widgets do not handle raw networking themselves. Instead, you declare required data sources (e.g. image URLs, iCal feeds) in the manifest, and the Zenso server securely fetches and passes the data into your Liquid template.

widget_sdk_quickstart.title: Widget SDK Quickstart
widget_sdk_quickstart.description: Create and preview your first custom widget in minutes using the plugin template and Vite plugin.
widget_sdk_quickstart.lead: Develop your first Zenso widget with live hot-reloading in less than five minutes.
widget_sdk_quickstart.step1_body:
Clone the official public starter repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zensoink/zenso-plugin-template.git my-widget
cd my-widget
pnpm install
```
widget_sdk_quickstart.step2_body:
Launch the local development environment powered by `@zenso/vite-plugin`:

```bash
pnpm dev
```

Open `http://localhost:5173` in your browser. You will see a live preview simulating your widget inside an actual e-paper canvas.
widget_sdk_quickstart.step3_body: Edit `mock/plugin.json` to simulate various states (e.g. long calendar titles, missing photos, network errors). Any edit to `index.liquid` or `style.css` updates instantly without reloading.

manifest_and_schemas.title: Manifest & Schemas
manifest_and_schemas.description: Define configuration forms, field types, and data sources using published schemas at schemas.zenso.ink.
manifest_and_schemas.lead: The `manifest.json` file describes your plugin to the Zenso platform and automatically generates user settings forms.
manifest_and_schemas.manifest_body:
All plugins validate against published JSON schemas hosted at `https://schemas.zenso.ink/v1/plugin-manifest.schema.json`.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://schemas.zenso.ink/v1/plugin-manifest.schema.json",
  "id": "com.example.greeting",
  "name": "Daily Greeting",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "entrypoint": "index.liquid"
}
```
manifest_and_schemas.fields_body:
Declare inputs in `config_schema` to let users customize the widget:
- `text`: Single-line text input
- `boolean`: Simple toggle switch
- `number`: Numeric input with optional `min` and `max`
- `color`: Color picker matching the e-paper palette
- `select`: Dropdown list with predefined options
manifest_and_schemas.sources_body: Use the `data_sources` block to declare external feeds. The platform fetches them server-side, preventing client CORS issues and isolating credentials.

building_and_publishing.title: Packaging & Installation
building_and_publishing.description: Package your widget into a distributable plugin.zip archive and upload it to the Zenso Panel.
building_and_publishing.lead: Once your widget is ready, bundle it into a distributable package and upload it to your Zenso panel.
building_and_publishing.build_body:
Run the build script:

```bash
pnpm build
```

This validates your manifest against `schemas.zenso.ink` and packages your assets into a single clean `plugin.zip` file in the `dist/` directory.
building_and_publishing.upload_body:
1. Navigate to **Plugins** in your Zenso Web Panel.
2. Click **Upload Plugin** and select your `plugin.zip` file.
3. The panel verifies the manifest and makes the widget immediately selectable in any screen layout slot.

overview.title: Hardware Architecture
overview.description: Inspect the Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3 microcontroller, EE04 baseboard, and power gating circuitry.
overview.lead: The physical Zenso frame blends precision Japanese electronic engineering with ultra-low-power embedded circuitry.
overview.mcu_body: The frame core is powered by the compact Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3 module, featuring a dual-core Xtensa 32-bit LX7 processor running at 240 MHz, integrated 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi (802.11 b/g/n), Bluetooth 5.0 LE, 8 MB PSRAM, and 8 MB SPI Flash.
overview.power_body: To deliver months of battery life, the custom EE04 carrier board incorporates a high-side MOSFET power gating circuit. Between refresh intervals, power to the display controller and external peripherals is physically severed, dropping overall standby current draw below 15 µA.
overview.fpc_body: The carrier board features a standard 50-pin 0.5mm pitch FPC receptacle compatible with Waveshare and Good Display raw panels, paired with an onboard TP4056/BQ-series Li-Ion charging controller and voltage divider connected to ADC GPIO for battery monitoring.

zenso_firmware.title: Open-Source Firmware
zenso_firmware.description: Build and flash the GPLv3 firmware with PlatformIO, and access the serial developer diagnostics console.
zenso_firmware.lead: Zenso firmware is fully open source under the **GNU General Public License v3 (GPLv3)**. It manages power cycling, Wi-Fi connectivity, and display updates.
zenso_firmware.build_body: Clone the official repository and open it in PlatformIO (VS Code or CLI):
zenso_firmware.serial_body: Open the PlatformIO serial monitor at 115200 baud (`pio device monitor`) to access the developer diagnostic interface:
zenso_firmware.license_body: You are free to audit, modify, and extend the firmware. If you distribute modified firmware binaries, you must make the corresponding source code publicly available under GPLv3.

byod_guide.title: BYOD Display Guide
byod_guide.description: Connect custom e-paper panels (Waveshare Spectra 6, ACeP, BWR, monochrome) and configure custom palettes.
byod_guide.lead: With Zenso's **Bring Your Own Device (BYOD)** program, makers can build custom smart frames using off-the-shelf electronic paper panels.
byod_guide.wiring_body: Connect your display's 50-pin or 24-pin FPC ribbon cable to the carrier board. Ensure the blue stiffener faces upward before locking the FPC flip-lock connector.
byod_guide.panel_config_body: In the Zenso Web Panel under **Device Settings -> Display Profile**, select **Custom BYOD**. Define your exact pixel dimensions (width/height), color depth (1bpp, 2bpp, or 4bpp), and assign your preferred color palette. The server will automatically render and quantize all widget screens to match your unique hardware specifications.
